headline: Highest risk is cascading error: OpenMetadata can ingest and act on upstream outputs via MCP/APIs, while the awesome-list agent is non-runnable and network-isolated, limiting direct injection and leakage.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a non-runnable awesome-list with no I/O surfaces and no network egress, so it cannot directly ingest B. Profile B exposes MCP/APIs/webhooks and can process external content, but there is no documented shared channel or parser path between them. The only plausible bridge is manual copy/paste or external orchestration, so severity stays low.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies B-generated content into a downstream parser for A-like content curation, prompt injection becomes possible.
IF a shared MCP or filesystem bridge is added between the pair, B-originated instructions could reach a consumer.
IF B is configured to treat untrusted text as instructions, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected; do not add shared clipboard or filesystem bridges.
Require manual review of any B output before reuse.
Disable any auto-execution of instructions embedded in metadata.
Use a strict allowlist for fields B may emit to downstream tools.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between producers and consumers.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no network egress, so it is not a leakage source. B touches governance, lineage, semantics, and memory/tribal knowledge and can call APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP, but the profiles do not show a shared workspace or sensitive regulated data. Leakage is therefore possible only through operator wiring, with small documented blast radius.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace containing sensitive metadata, B may transmit it through its API/MCP surfaces.
IF B is granted credentials to external systems, its touched metadata can leave the local boundary.
IF A is repurposed into a content source with hidden sensitive text, manual transfer could leak it.
mitigations: Do not place sensitive files in any shared workspace.
Restrict B credentials to least privilege.
Review outbound API/webhook destinations in B.
Keep A as a static reference list only.
requires-engineering: add DLP or egress allowlisting.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write, network, or runtime surfaces and is not runnable, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. B supports multiple instances and has API/MCP/event/webhook surfaces, but no shared writable directory, git state, or overlapping OAuth scope is documented. The pair therefore has only a limited conflict risk unless an operator adds shared mutable resources.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory or database, write conflicts can occur.
IF B is configured to mutate shared metadata without locking, concurrent instances may race.
IF an orchestrator maps both agents to the same OAuth principal, scope collisions become possible.
mitigations: Avoid shared writable directories.
Run only one B instance per mutable resource.
Separate credentials per agent.
Use external locking for any shared state.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a curated reference source, and B is a runnable metadata platform with APIs/MCP/webhooks that can consume upstream content. If B treats A-derived content as authoritative, errors or stale recommendations can cascade into metadata, lineage, or governance actions. The pathway is inferred rather than directly documented, so medium is appropriate and uncertainty is resolved upward from low.
conditions: IF B ingests A-derived recommendations without verification, stale or incorrect metadata can propagate.
IF B uses A as a source of governance or lineage facts, downstream records may be wrong.
IF an operator automates A-to-B ingestion, B may act on unverified content.
mitigations: Require human review before importing A-derived content into B.
Mark A as non-authoritative reference material.
Add validation rules for imported metadata.
Log provenance on every imported field.
requires-engineering: implement verification gates before B writes downstream records.

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data class, residency mismatch, or retention conflict is documented for either agent. A touches no data classes and is non-runnable; B lists governance-related metadata but no PHI, EU PII, or special compliance boundary. With no evidence of a compliance-sensitive flow, the pairwise compliance risk is provably absent from the profiles provided.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is later introduced into B, compliance review becomes necessary.
IF an operator configures cross-border storage or retention policies, a new compliance risk may appear.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document retention settings for B.
Review any future residency requirements before onboarding sensitive data.
Maintain separate environments for regulated workloads.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
